name: get_document_version
description: Get a draft version of a document: its Markdown, its status and its provenance manifest, the exact fact versions and source passages that it cites. An approved version never changes: write a new draft from the Markdown, cite the current fact versions of get_event_profile, and propose it with propose_changeset. An upload version has no Markdown and is not found here.

version_id.description: The ID of a draft version, from `list_documents`.

CitedFactView.description: An exact fact version that a draft cites. get_event_profile gives the current version of the fact.

dispute_notes.description: The dispute notes about the fact version (ADR 0073), oldest first: a person objects to it. Empty if there is none.

CitedPassageView.description: A passage that a draft cites. get_source_passage gives its text.

DisputeNoteView.description: A dispute note: the objection of a person to a fact version or to a source (ADR 0073).

ManifestView.description: The fact versions and source passages that a draft version cites (ADR 0051).

dispute_notes.description: The dispute notes about the version (ADR 0073), oldest first: a person objects to it. Empty if there is none.

redacted.description: True after a legal redaction: the Markdown is gone (ADR 0072).

status.description: `draft`, `review`, `approved`, `superseded` or `archived`. An approved version never changes.

name: get_event_profile
description: Get what the team plans for an event: the accepted facts, the assumptions, the unknowns, the open questions and the open proposals, each in its own list. Each fact names its version and the source passages that support it. A field without a fact is not listed: compare with get_event_schema to see which fields nobody has addressed yet. Only accepted facts are confirmed. Never fill in an unknown, and never present an assumption or an open proposal as accepted.

event_key.description: The key of the event, for example `FLY28`, from `list_events`.

AuthorView.description: Who did something, for which member and through which channel (ADR 0039).

channel.description: `web`, `telegram`, `job`, `api-token` or `cli`. The list of channels is open.

id.description: The user ID of a member or an AI client, or the ID of a service identity.

kind.description: `member`, `service` or `ai`. The list of kinds is open.

principal_id.description: The member for whom the author acts, if the author is not that member.

DisputeNoteView.description: A dispute note: the objection of a person to a fact version or to a source (ADR 0073).

EvidenceView.description: A passage of a source version that supports a fact version.

captured_at.description: RFC 3339. The time when tada captured the source version.

dispute_notes.description: The dispute notes about it (ADR 0073), oldest first: a person objects to it. Empty if there is none.

end.description: The offset after the last character.

page.description: The page of a PDF, from 1.

quote.description: Empty after a legal redaction of the source (ADR 0072).

redacted.description: True after a legal redaction of the source: the quote is empty (ADR 0072).

start.description: The offset of the first character, in characters of the normalized text.

FactView.description: The current version of a fact with a value.

accepted_at.description: RFC 3339. The time of the acceptance of the current fact version.

accepted_by.description: The reviewer who accepted the current fact version.

approximate.description: True for an approximate value, for example "about 20,000".

dispute_notes.description: The dispute notes about it (ADR 0073), oldest first: a person objects to it. Empty if there is none.

redacted.description: True after a legal redaction: the value is gone (ADR 0072).

version.description: The number of the current fact version.

expected_version.description: The fact version that the proposal expects. Absent if the field had no fact.

OpenQuestionView.description: An open question of the event.

owner_user_id.description: The user ID of the member who owns the question.

redacted.description: True after a legal redaction: the text is gone (ADR 0072).

accepted_by.description: The reviewer who accepted the current fact version.

dispute_notes.description: The dispute notes about it (ADR 0073), oldest first: a person objects to it. Empty if there is none.

ValueInput.description:
A fact value. Its type must match the value type of the field.
The read tools give values in the same shape (ADR 0040).

oneOf.description:
A decimal number or range in the unit of the field, as text, for example `"20000"` or `"1.5"`.
A single value has `min` equal to `max`.
An amount or range in the minor unit of the currency of the field, for example 1500 for CHF 15.00.
A date as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

name: get_event_schema
description: Get the field catalog of an event: the active fields with their meaning and the JSON Schema of their values, and the kinds of records. Use an existing field first; propose a new field only if no field has the meaning.

statuses.description: The statuses of a record of this kind. Empty for a kind without a status.

label.description: The German label of a field of the event. A shipped field has its label in the web client only.

value_schema.description: The JSON Schema of the `value` of a fact of this field.

catalog_version.description: The version of the shipped `core` catalog.

fields.description: The active fields. A deprecated field is closed for new facts, so the list leaves it out.

name: get_source_passage
description: Get the exact text of a range of a source version, to quote it in a citation. The offsets count characters, as in the evidence of a fact and in a search hit.

end.description: The offset after the last character. A passage has at most 10000 characters.

start.description: The offset of the first character, in characters of the normalized text.

name: list_actions
description: List the actions of an event, each with its owner, status and the evidence of the accepted proposals that made it. The list holds at most 200 records, in the order of their numbers, and has no next page. If more is true, the event has more actions than this tool can show: tell the member.

status.description: Only the actions with this status.

milestone_id.description: The ID of the milestone of the action, from `list_milestones`.

redacted.description: True after a legal redaction: the texts are empty (ADR 0072).

name: list_commitments

Never treat a condition as met without evidence. The list holds at most 200 records, in the order of their numbers, and has no next page. If more is true, the event has more commitments than this tool can show: tell the member.

status.description: Only the commitments with this status.

condition.description:
The condition of a conditional promise. It stays after the commitment becomes firm.
A condition is met only when evidence says so.

redacted.description: True after a legal redaction: the texts are empty (ADR 0072).

True after a legal redaction: the texts are empty (ADR 0072).

name: list_documents
description: List the documents of an event, the newest first, each with its readable ID, its record version and its newest version. A version is an upload (a file) or a draft (Markdown). To propose a new draft version of a document, send its version as expected_version. The list holds at most the 200 newest documents and has no next page. If more is true, the event has older documents that this tool cannot show: tell the member.

event_key.description: The key of the event, for example `FLY28`, from `list_events`.

DocumentSummaryView.description: A document with its newest version.

redacted.description: True after a legal redaction: the name is gone (ADR 0072).

version.description: The record version of the document. A draft of this document expects it as `expected_version`.

VersionSummaryView.description: One version of a document. Only a draft has a status and Markdown; an upload is a file.

redacted.description: True after a legal redaction: the file or the Markdown is gone (ADR 0072).

status.description: The status of a draft: `draft`, `review`, `approved`, `superseded` or `archived`. Absent for an upload.

name: list_events
description: List the events that the member can read, in the order of their keys. The other tools take the key. The result also holds caller_user_id, the user ID of the member: use it as owner to assign work to the member. The list holds at most 200 events and has no next page. If more is true, the member can read more events than this tool can show: tell the member.

EventView.description: An event that the caller can read.

event_key.description: The short key of the event, for example `FLY28`. The other tools take it.

time_zone.description: The IANA time zone of the event.

caller_user_id.description:
The user ID of the member who uses the tool. Use it as `owner` to assign work to this member;
`list_members` gives the user IDs of the other members of an event.

more.description: True if the caller can read more events than the list shows.

name: list_members
description: List the members of an event with their user ID, display name and event role, in the order of the names. Use the user ID as owner of an open question, an action or a commitment: a member with the event role event-manager or event-contributor can own work. An owner or admin of the organization can also own work; this list holds only the event members. The user ID of the member who uses the tool is caller_user_id of list_events.

event_key.description: The key of the event, for example `FLY28`, from `list_events`.

EventMemberView.description:
A member of an event: what each reader of the event also sees in the web client.
It has no email address.

event_role.description: `event-manager`, `event-contributor` or `event-viewer`. A member with one of the first two can own work; an owner or admin of the organization can also own work without an event role.

user_id.description: The user ID. Use it as `owner` of a question, action or commitment.

name: list_milestones
description: List the milestones of an event: the dates that its plan holds, each with its owner, status, warnings and the evidence of the accepted proposals that made it. An action can name one milestone. The list holds at most 200 records, in the order of their numbers, and has no next page. If more is true, the event has more milestones than this tool can show: tell the member.

event_key.description: The key of the event, for example `FLY28`, from `list_events`.

status.description: Only the milestones with this status.

DisputeNoteView.description: A dispute note: the objection of a person to a fact version or to a source (ADR 0073).

EvidenceItem.description: A passage that supports one version of a record, from a source that the member can read.

dispute_notes.description: The dispute notes about the source (ADR 0073), oldest first: a person objects to it. Empty if there is none.

quote.description: Empty after a legal redaction of the source (ADR 0072).

redacted.description: True after a legal redaction of the source: the quote is empty (ADR 0072).
True after a legal redaction: the texts are empty (ADR 0072).

WarningItem.description: A warning about a milestone at the time of the read.

An action of the milestone is open, in progress or blocked, and it is due after the date of the milestone.

more.description: True if the event has more milestones than the list shows.

name: list_workstreams
description: List the workstreams of an event: its areas of work, each with its lead. A work record names a workstream by its ID. Propose a record in an active workstream, or in a new workstream of the same changeset (create-workstream); a closed workstream takes no new records.

event_key.description: The key of the event, for example `FLY28`, from `list_events`.

lead_user_id.description: The member who leads the workstream.

redacted.description: True after a legal redaction: the texts are empty (ADR 0072).

status.description: `active` or `closed`. A closed workstream takes no new records.

name: propose_changeset
description: Propose changes for the member to review. Nothing changes until a reviewer accepts a proposal in the Review Inbox of tada; no tool accepts, rejects or deletes. Only a `propose` token of a member who can propose in the event can propose. One changeset holds one intake: source_text is the member's own words of this intake, and the proposals are the changes that these words support. If the member said nothing new and the proposals rest only on stored sources, leave source_text out: never write words in the member's name. Each passage then names its source_version_id, and the reason of each proposal holds your explanation. event_id comes from list_events; leave it out only for a changeset that creates new events. The input schema names the kinds of operations and the rules of each field, for example the links of a document draft. Use an existing field of get_event_schema first. Never guess a value: propose an unknown instead. Take the expected_version of a fact and the fact versions that a draft cites from get_event_profile, and the expected_version of a document from list_documents. To change a draft, read it with get_document_version and propose a new version. Each proposal cites at least one passage as evidence: of source_text, or of another source version that the member can read in the event, for example a hit of search_sources. Always send a new UUIDv7 as the id of the changeset and of each proposal. To retry, send the same changeset with the same ids again. If a check fails, tada stores nothing: the result has isError, the problem code and, for validation-failed, each invalid value as a JSON pointer and a code.

ChoiceInput.description: One choice of a new choice field.

label.description: The German label of the choice.

oneOf.description: A new document of the event.

id.description: The UUIDv7 of the new document.

name.description: The name of the document, 1 to 200 characters.

expected_version.description: The current version of the document.

reason.description: A short reason for the proposal. The words of the agent go here, never into `source_text`.

field_id.description: A field of the event catalog, or a new field of the same changeset.

label.description: The German label that people see.

field_id.description: A field of the event, or a new field of the same changeset.

label.description: The German label of the choice.

oneOf.description: Close a field of the event for new facts.
Create an open question with its owner.

markdown.description:
CommonMark with tables, UTF-8, one sentence per line. No raw HTML and no images.
A fact is an empty link to an exact fact version: `[](tada:fact/<fact-uuid>?v=<n>)`.
Never write the value of a fact as text.
A source passage is a link with the supporting words: `[words](tada:source/<source-version-uuid>#<start>-<end>)`.
A `tada:` link writes each UUID in lowercase with hyphens. Other links use `https` or `mailto` only.
Each link must cite an accepted fact version, an assumption or an unknown of the event, never an open proposal,
or a source version that the member can see.
A number, date or amount outside a `tada:` link gives a lint warning for the reviewer.

oneOf.description:
Create a person of the organization. Search the persons first: propose a new one only if none matches.
A person belongs to no event, so the operation has no `event_id`.

id.description: The UUIDv7 of the new person.

oneOf.description:
Create an institution of the organization. Search the institutions first: propose a new one only if none matches.
An institution belongs to no event, so the operation has no `event_id`.

id.description: The UUIDv7 of the new institution.

institution_kind.description: `kind` names the operation, so the kind of the institution has this name.

oneOf.description: Create an action of the event. It starts `open`.

id.description: The UUIDv7 of the new action.

milestone.description:
A milestone of the event that is not canceled, or a new milestone of the same changeset;
then the proposal depends on the proposal that creates it.

owner.description: The user ID of a member with the contributor or manager role in the event.

start_date.description: The start date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. It is not after the due date.

workstream.description:
An active workstream of the event, or a new workstream of this changeset;
then the proposal depends on the proposal that creates it.

oneOf.description:
Create a commitment of the event. With a condition it starts `conditional`, else `firm`.
Never invent a signature or an approval: a commitment with an open condition stays conditional.

condition.description: The condition of the promise, 1 to 500 characters, for example "subject to a signed order".

id.description: The UUIDv7 of the new commitment.

owner.description: The user ID of the member who follows the commitment up: a contributor or manager of the event.

promisor.description:
The person or institution that promises. It can be a new person or institution of the same changeset;
then the proposal depends on the proposal that creates it.

text.description: What the promisor promises, 1 to 500 characters.

workstream.description:
An active workstream of the event, or a new workstream of this changeset;
then the proposal depends on the proposal that creates it.

oneOf.description: Change the status of an action of the event.

expected_version.description: The current version of the action.

oneOf.description: Set or clear the due date of an action of the event.

due_date.description: The new due date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Leave it out to clear the due date.

expected_version.description: The current version of the action.

oneOf.description:
Change the status of a commitment of the event.
`firm` means that the condition is met; the evidence must show it, for example the signed order.
The reason of the proposal becomes the reason of the firm commitment, so it has at most 500 characters.

expected_version.description: The current version of the commitment.

oneOf.description:
Create a workstream of the event: a named part with a lead, to group the actions and commitments of the event.
Actions and commitments of the same changeset can name it; then they depend on this proposal.
Only the event managers review it.

id.description: The UUIDv7 of the new workstream.

lead.description: The user ID of a member with the contributor or manager role in the event.

name.description:
1 to 200 characters. No other workstream of the event has this name, whatever its case.
`list_workstreams` shows the existing names. A closed workstream keeps its name.

oneOf.description: Create a milestone of the event: a date that the plan of the event holds. It starts `open`.

id.description: The UUIDv7 of the new milestone.

owner.description: The user ID of a member with the contributor or manager role in the event.

workstream.description: An active workstream of the event.

oneOf.description:
Change the status of a milestone of the event.
`open` changes to `reached` or `canceled`; `reached` changes back to `open`; `canceled` is final.

expected_version.description: The current version of the milestone.

oneOf.description: Set or clear the milestone of an action of the event.

expected_version.description: The current version of the action.

milestone.description:
A milestone of the event that is not canceled, or a new milestone of the same changeset.

page.description: The page of a PDF, from 1.

The source version of the passage. Leave it out for the source text of the changeset.

for example a text file that a member uploaded to the event.
A changeset without a source text needs it on each passage, else the code is `no-source-text`.

start.description: The offset of the first character.

ValueInput.description:
A fact value. Its type must match the value type of the field.
The read tools give values in the same shape (ADR 0040).

oneOf.description:
A decimal number or range in the unit of the field, as text, for example `"20000"` or `"1.5"`.
A single value has `min` equal to `max`.
An amount or range in the minor unit of the currency of the field, for example 1500 for CHF 15.00.
A date as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

unit.description: The `snake_case` key of the unit, for example `person_per_day`.

granularity.description: Leave it out to accept each granularity.

multiple.description: True if a fact can hold several choices.

event_id.description:
The event of all proposals. A changeset without an event belongs to the organization:
it creates new events, and its other proposals work in these new events.

id.description:
The UUIDv7 of the new changeset. Send a new one, so that a retry with the same id is safe.
Without it, tada makes one, and a retry after a lost response is refused.

source_text.description:
The member's own words. tada stores them as a source version.
The passages count characters (Unicode scalar values) of this text after normalization: Unicode NFC with `\n` line ends.
At most 100,000 characters after the normalization.
Leave it out, or send it empty, if the member said nothing new and the proposals rest only on stored
source versions (ADR 0079). Never write words in the name of the member. Each passage then names its
`source_version_id`. A text of white space only counts as empty.

name: search_sources
description: Search the source texts that the member can read, for example the words of members and documents. Each hit names its source version and a snippet with its offsets. Cite a hit as a passage: source_version_id, start and end.
